_comment: Judgment rows of the domain-model score - the ones no grep settles. Re-record them by running the /domain-driven-design review and editing this file; editing it IS the re-recording, because scripts/domain-score.mjs measures staleness from when this file was last touched relative to the Core modules. A row is reported stale, and drops out of the verified score, when a Core module was touched more recently. Structural rows are not recorded here: they are re-checked from the tree on every run.
reviewer: /domain-modeling re-record after the refusal-footer change touched the Core module settle.ts. What recovery pointer a mode's refusals carry was re-decided at every return site: worktree hand-wrote the integration-branch footer eight times, and the two refusals that commit resolved conflicts and review fixes — both firing after integrationCreated, so the finally keeps the branch on disk — shipped telling users to inspect a retained branch they never named. Settle gains decorateFooter, the exact parallel of the decorateDetails extension point workflow already uses: worktree registers the pointer once, immediately after the branch exists, and every subsequent refusal — including ones written later — carries it. refuse also absorbed the model-visible cap, which loop and orchestrate had each independently reinvented as capping the formatted-error-plus-footer and slicing the formatted prefix back off for refuse to re-prepend; the settle-level test pins that the capped whole refuse now produces is byte-identical to what the slice trick assembled. One design choice is deliberate and recorded: the registered footer lands after the cap, not inside it, because it is the short recovery pointer a truncated refusal needs most — capping it with the body would let a pathological cause swallow the pointer, recreating the defect in exactly the corner where recovery matters. The footer is refusal vocabulary only; complete's text stays the mode's own. The review's watch-item was checked, not worsened: no new early return was added between retainFailureState's set sites and the finally that reads it. All seven new tests were verified load-bearing by reverting the fix (7/7 fail; the two worktree tests drive the real handler over real git to the exact commit-failure refusals). No aggregate, transition, or field changed — Settle keeps its construction path and tracked-run invariant, and the footer is behavior on the object that owns refusal text, not exposed data — so small-aggregates, behavior-rich, domain-events, depth-rich-core, and depth-invariants-in-aggregates stand as re-derived; the CONTEXT.md Settle entry now names both decorators and the cap ownership, and no competing vocabulary shipped, so depth-language-consistency stands. The two-axis review round then tightened one thing and declined two: the registered footer's exemption from the cap was a prose-only bound (refuse's JSDoc promised a cap the mode's closure could exceed at will), so it now has its own small byte allowance and the whole refusal is structurally bounded, pinned by test; decorateFooter keeps the card's name rather than the suggested registerRefusalFooter, because its registration semantics (latest wins, applied to every subsequent output) are exactly decorateDetails' and the pair reads as one extension-point vocabulary; and the recovery pointer stays a plain string closure rather than gaining a type, because it is one rendered line with no rule of its own to own. PR review (Codex) then found the consolidation's own planted defect, on schedule: capping the assembled prefix truncates from the tail, and formatFlowError places the Retryable/Fix/Code lines after the cause — so a worktree refusal built over megabytes of git stderr, previously uncapped and complete, would now lose exactly the structured suffix a reader recovers by. The cause, the one unbounded FlowError field, is now bounded first (REFUSAL_CAUSE_CAP, half the model-visible cap, so it can never starve the suffix or a per-call footer entirely) and the bound is model-visible only — details and trace evidence keep the error object uncut, pinned by test. loop/orchestrate byte-identity is unaffected: their causes are short literals the bound returns untouched. Codex's second round showed the cause was not in fact the only unbounded field — schema.ts puts no length bound on worktree.baseRef and the handler interpolates the invalid value into the refusal message — so the per-field bound now covers all three variable-length fields (message, cause, fix), with allowances chosen to sum under the model-visible cap: the suffix's survival is arithmetic over named constants rather than an enumeration of which call sites interpolate what, which is the property that makes the next unbounded interpolation someone writes already handled. The tempting alternative — reassembling the formatted layout in refuse to cap head and keep tail — was rejected as a Mirror of formatFlowError's layout. Prior record: /domain-modeling re-record after the strict-trace structural gate touched the Core modules trace-scope.ts, trace-sink.ts, trace.ts, and flow.ts. Trace health had been carrying two questions under one word. It is a writer's count — spans the sink attempted against spans that reached the file, incremented inside append() — so it is answered while writing and is structurally blind to anything only a reader can see. traceStructure() could always answer the other question (root reachability, interval containment, duplicate ids, surplus rows) but had exactly one caller, the read-back report; strictTraceError's own fix text sent users to `npm run trace:report -- --strict` to do by hand what the gate would not. A run staking its verdict on evidence was the one caller never checking it. CONTEXT.md gains Trace structure as a term distinct from Trace health, with each on the other's Avoid list, because folding them would let a strict run certify evidence nothing read. The verdict rides on FlowTraceLink as its own optional member — absent means unverified, never verified-fine — rather than collapsing into the health status, whose root-span attribute is necessarily written before the file can be read back and would otherwise disagree with the link. No second validator was written: the read-back composes parseTraceJsonl and traceStructure, so the gate and the report answer from one derivation. Ordinary flows do not read anything back. One fence was found and left standing: runner.ts deliberately writes no child span for a run that spawned nothing ('never a child span for a child that did not run'), so the tempting expectation 'every settled run owes a span' was rejected rather than enforced. The plan-derived owed-event set the review suggested was also rejected: waves list roles rather than spawns and carry no event kinds, so deriving one would have added a Mirror of handler behavior — the anti-pattern CONTEXT.md names — in the module whose job is telling the truth about what happened. Codex review then found sixteen more, all fixed. The sixteenth made the strict gate enforce the contract the fifteenth documented: absent structure means unverified, and strictTraceError now refuses a link nothing read back instead of trusting that flow.ts's wiring (verify: traceStrict) is the only way strict and unverified could meet. Latent — the wired path always verifies — but a gate that documents a rule and enforces it only by convention is the two-readers split in miniature. The fifteenth drew no coordination logic at all — FlowTraceStructure was missing from types.ts's trace re-exports and details.trace.structure was undocumented in flow-reference, the AGENTS.md sync rule again — which is itself evidence the protocol reached its fixpoint: the last defect standing was the public surface not yet describing it. The fourteenth was the reconciliation's own mirror: a final reading that fails after a positive certification landed left the file claiming verified while the live call refused, and a cleared read error later let reports honor a certification that covered only the preliminary reading. The sink now appends a best-effort revocation in that corner, and the reserved slot makes even its bare arrival durable — one surplus row withholds on completeness before any reader sees the flag. The window that remains, a read and a write failing together, is one an append-only record cannot close from inside, and the code says so where it stops. The thirteenth closed the dual reading's own disagreement window: a transient failure on the preliminary reading writes a durable revocation, and the live verdict must not out-vote the record it wrote when the final reading recovers. reconcileVerdicts makes the precedence a pure rule — a preliminary failure stands, a final failure stands, agreement passes through — pinned as a unit test because the divergence is only reachable through I/O faults nothing in-process can fake deterministically. This supersedes the fault-text ordering pin from the round before: with precedence honored, the post-write reading's verdict only surfaces on I/O faults, so the surplus fault names the preliminary yardstick again. The last two close the remaining criterion splits. The report's own verified-outcome line was withholding on structural validity alone while its incompleteTraces used the full disjunction, so a certified trace that later gained a surplus row counted as a verified outcome in the same report that refused it as incomplete; the outcome now withholds on the one completeness predicate, computed once. And the verdict the link carries is now read after the finalize's last write: the first reading only decides what the certification event may truthfully record, and a second reading over the final state — every row now expected, attempted equal to declared — is what the link reports, so a path rotated between the reading and the append lands as missing rows rather than as a pass against a file that no longer exists. Both pinned load-bearing, the second by the fault text naming the post-write yardstick. The tenth was the verifier accepting by a subset of the report's criteria: structure.invalid covers connectivity, attribution, and containment, but duplicates, id-less rows, and surplus are separate counters in the report's disjunction, and the verifier checked none of them — so a surplus row from a concurrent writer under the same trace id (the #127 shape) passed the live gate and failed the downstream report. The acceptance now mirrors the report's disjunction exactly, which is the property this whole change exists to provide: one criterion, two readers. The ninth was the counter half of the reserved slot: the root's observed_spans was computed before the certification lands, so a healthy strict trace persisted expected=N, observed=N-1 while the link said N/N — a false missing-span signal to any OTel consumer and a breach of flow-reference's same-counters contract. The certification is now counted the way the root already counts itself, optimistically in the write that precedes it, so both root counters share one convention and match the link on the healthy path; either append's own failure stays with the link and the file's shortfall, as it always did for the root's. The last two named the root cause the earlier rounds kept colliding with: the root freezes the span count before verification can run, so the certification row itself was a span beyond the declaration — every healthy strict trace failed the read-back report gate — and its bare depends_on_span_ids read as corruption to dependenciesHold, invalidating the very tree it certified. The fix is the reserved slot Codex proposed: a verifying root declares expectedSpans + 1, so a landed certification matches the declaration exactly and a missing one leaves the trace short, which reads as loss — failing closed. The event now carries no dependency attributes; its parentage is the whole relationship. The verifier takes both yardsticks (rows attempted when it reads, count the root declares) since it runs between the two. The last two are one lesson learned twice: a correction that has to be written is not durable, because the write that carries it fails in exactly the conditions that made it necessary. The design inverted — a strict root now declares its claims contingent in the same write that makes them, and a reader honours them only on positive certification. Every way the certification can fail to arrive, including its append failing, now reads as unverified rather than verified; the negative event survives as the diagnostic naming the fault, not as the mechanism. The last one is the sharpest: the revocation event that corrects the root depends on another successful append, and append is best-effort, so a disk that filled after the root was written loses the evidence and the correction together. The report now derives the verdict from the rows themselves — traceStructure was already computed there — and keeps the revocation as the second, independent check for a fault only the writer could see, such as a rewritten expectation these rows alone look consistent with. Neither correction depends on the other. The most serious repeated the fault #125 had just removed: the root is written before the export can be read back, so a strict run whose structure failed still had `flow.outcome_verified` on disk and trace reports counted it as verified. An exported span is immutable, so the correction takes the shape the codebase already uses for a revoked budget wrap-up — a linked event, applied by the reader — and trace-report.ts now honours it. A filesystem error from the read was also being returned verbatim into details, which names the absolute path the AGENTS.md redaction invariant exists to keep out. The read-back additionally cross-checks the persisted root's declared expectation against what the run attempted, since corruption of that attribute is exactly what the reading is for; and it parses only the lines carrying its own trace id, because in the eval setup one file accumulates every flow and re-parsing all of it each finalize costs more with every call. Reading a finished export back moved to its own module (trace-verify.ts) rather than raise the 500-line cap the extraction avoided: the writer checking its own work was the wrong shape anyway. Review of the change corrected it twice more. The read-back was validating the whole JSONL file rather than the flow's own trace_id, so the second flow in a shared trace file — the normal eval setup — was refused for a surplus that was its predecessor's rows; it is now scoped the way the read-back report groups. And makeTraceSink's sixth positional parameter became a TraceSinkOptions object, because reaching `verify` meant passing two `undefined`s. One residual is documented rather than fixed: stableTraceIds derives an id from trace context and mode, so two calls sharing both write two roots under one id and the reading cannot tell them apart. What the change does NOT do is also recorded, in the changelog and here: it does not make trace health see an un-emitted coordination event, because the expectation it measures against is still what the sink attempted. No aggregate, transition, or field changed; small-aggregates, behavior-rich, domain-events, and depth-invariants-in-aggregates stand as re-derived. depth-rich-core and depth-language-consistency are updated below. Prior record: /domain-modeling re-record after the run-state change touched the Core modules run.ts, sanitize.ts, flow.ts, and trace.ts. One run's state had three derivations: isFailed (sanitize.ts) read exitCode + stopReason, entryResultFailed (ui-flow-card.ts) read exitCode + errorCode, and ui-gantt.ts carried a third inline copy of the card's. The second disjuncts were disjoint, and ui.ts populates the persisted errorCode from result.error?.code only, so a child reporting stopReason:'error' with no diagnostic (runner.ts copies the child's stop reason verbatim; the provider branch needs an errorMessage too, so with exit 0 the classification cascade falls through) rendered failed in the live row, partial in the card header, and complete in that same card's row. CONTEXT.md gains Run state, and Settled gains the code home it never had: run.ts now owns runState/runSettled/runFailed, structural over both shapes one run takes, and ui-style.ts re-exports the RunState type rather than declaring a second copy. isFailed keeps its name and its liveness-unaware contract — what a handler wants about a run it just settled — and is widened to read the error under either name, which is what makes it total over the persisted projection too; the fence was not load-bearing (1018 tests unchanged). The liveness sentinel exitCode === -1 was spelled out at ten sites, two of them Core (flow.ts, trace.ts); it is now spelled once, in runSettled, so no surface has to know an exit integer is also a liveness flag. flowAgentState moves out of inspector.ts — the canonical four-state derivation had been stranded in the most specialized view, which is why ui-live-row.ts reached sideways for it and the card could not use it at all. tests/run-state.test.ts is the check none of the surfaces had: each had passing tests of its own and nothing asserted they agreed. Verified load-bearing by restoring the old predicate — three of its six tests fail. No aggregate, transition, or field changed: Run keeps its transitions and its private state, and FlowRunResult stays the plain read projection, so small-aggregates, behavior-rich, domain-events, and depth-invariants-in-aggregates stand as re-derived. depth-language-consistency is updated below. Prior record: /domain-modeling re-record after the mode pre-spawn refusal change touched the Core module validate.ts. The per-mode refusals validate.ts mirrored (the fan-out cap, the graph cycle, monitor's probe validation) moved onto the Supporting mode table as `preSpawnRefusal` declarations each handler now calls, so a rule and its mirror became one function; validate.ts keeps only the Core-owned predicates those declarations build on (validGraphNodes, graphDependsOn) and the workflow phase rules it re-exports from validate-workflow.ts. Nothing enforced changed: every refusal keeps its code, and the messages the eval reads are byte-identical, verified by a differential check over 18 representative calls (one cause is deliberately more precise — a graph with no dependency-free node now says so, instead of borrowing the wave loop's mid-run wording), and tests/mode-prespawn-refusal.test.ts deep-compares each handler's refusal to its declaration rather than merely matching codes — a check that would have failed before this change, because parallel's handler and its mirror gave different causes for the same TOO_MANY_TASKS. Cross-referencing the glossary against the change found two language faults in the change itself, both fixed before recording. (1) It claimed the bare phrase 'pre-spawn refusal' for the narrow mode-declared concept, though six existing sites (runner-budget.ts, preset-approval.ts, and four tests) already use that phrase for any refusal before spawning, an Admission gate's and a Budget's included; the entry is now Mode pre-spawn refusal, with the bare phrase on its Avoid list. (2) It shipped two words for one concept — 'pre-spawn declaration' in the mode files against 'pre-spawn refusal' on the table — now swept to the latter across the six mode files and the test. CONTEXT.md also sharpens Mirror to say that a mirror is a second derivation which must be kept in agreement with the first, and to prefer a declaration where one is possible. No aggregate, transition, or field changed, so small-aggregates, behavior-rich, domain-events, and depth-invariants-in-aggregates stand as re-derived; depth-rich-core and depth-language-consistency are updated below. Prior record: The fleet-panel removal touched flow.ts once more after this record: one JSDoc sentence was reworded ('a dead flow never lingers on the fleet as live' -> 'in the live-flow registry') because the Fleet glossary entry and the fleet panel were removed. Documentation wording only - no transition, field, or rule changed, so every judgment verdict below stands as re-derived; fleet-panel.ts also leaves the adapters list because the module is deleted. Prior note: PR #109 review feedback touched run.ts once more after this record: a JSDoc sentence was reworded for grammar ("Retain, in its stored (capture-policy) form, …"). Documentation wording only — no transition, field, or rule changed, so every judgment verdict below stands as re-derived. Original basis: /domain-modeling re-record after the wrap-up-notice change (#106, commit 3c10cbb) touched budget.ts, delegation.ts, and run.ts. Two Core concepts had shipped unnamed and under three competing words ('rejected', 'salvageable', 'unvalidated'), so CONTEXT.md gains Rejected envelope and Unvalidated claims under Contracts and handoffs. Cross-referencing the glossary against the code found the stated invariant stronger than the enforced one: validateEnvelopeAgainstContract checked conformance before integrity, so a strict-schema miss returned salvageable:true without validateDigests ever running, and an artifact escaping the child cwd or failing its digest could be surfaced as findings. The check order is now attribution → integrity → conformance and is documented as the invariant it is; the discriminator was renamed salvageable → claimsSurfaceable so the code speaks the new entries; tests/preset-code-review.test.ts covers the two previously unreachable cases (uncontained artifact + schema miss, digest mismatch + schema miss); and the coordination fault is a manifest entry (corrupted-artifact-digest-under-schema-miss, sharing a factory with corrupted-artifact-digest) rather than a bespoke test. Error-code precedence moved only for a digest mismatch arriving with a schema miss (now RETURN_DIGEST_MISMATCH); the other integrity failures keep RETURN_ENVELOPE_INVALID and change only which cause they report. Budget's WRAP_UP_FRACTION/wrapUpNotice and Run's rejected-envelope retention were reviewed against the behavior-rich and small-aggregates rows and change neither verdict. Prior context: bash-ro change incl. PR #102 review rounds 1-4 + OS-sandbox pivot (Generic bash-readonly-sandbox.ts wraps bash-ro children in sandbox-exec denying cwd writes as the security boundary; bash-readonly.ts gains the pure enforcement-decision predicate and hardened allowlist screens; runner wraps the invocation and records the enforcing layer) (re-derived against the Core module bash-readonly.ts: a zero-import vocabulary object owning the bash-ro token — env marker, toolset split, and allowlist predicate — so parent classification and child enforcement cannot drift; validate.ts changes are message-only (attribution and fix text name the token, verdicts unchanged, pinned by tests/shared-write-guidance.test.ts). Other verdicts carried from the #100 re-record and the 2026-07-31 /domain-driven-design review)

small-aggregates.label: Aggregates are small (one root + minimal cluster)
small-aggregates.note: Flow (flow.ts) is the aggregate root CONTEXT.md promised: one bounded delegation whose lifecycle is the explicit typed progression refused → admitted → dispatched → settled. The root stays small by owning ordering only — every pre-spawn gate is a supplied predicate/approval object walked in the aggregate's declared order, and Budget, the handoff consumer, and the trace sink remain separate objects the root holds references to. Run (run.ts) is the one root over a child result's lifecycle. index.ts execute() is a composition root again: it adapts ctx/ui/liveFlows/session persistence into the aggregate's ports and hands over (#97). The residue #100 named is resolved: the aggregate carries the one ResolvedCall (post-preset params, policy, preset) and hands it to ports as arguments — resolvePreset is pure, the details builder is constructed once from the resolution, preset formatting comes back from preparation — so no port in execute() assigns a local another port reads (tests/flow-capture-ownership.test.ts).

behavior-rich.label: Domain objects contain behavior, not just data
behavior-rich.note: Budget owns its rule. DelegationContract's transitions live on ResolvedDelegationContract, and receipt consumption exists only on ApprovalAuthorization — the capability verify returns, bound to the verified consumer (PR #98 review). The residue named by #97 is resolved: an envelope or handoff now attaches to a result only through Run.acceptReturnEnvelope / Run.acceptHandoff (run.ts), and what sanitize.ts held as two module-level WeakMap side-channels is now ECMAScript-private state of the one Run object per result, with consume-once semantics (the envelope candidate is capped on capture, discarded on failure, and taken exactly once). This is encapsulation behind domain transitions, not field privacy: FlowRunResult deliberately stays the plain, writable read projection the views and the runner fill (exit codes, usage, durations), and the identity lookup Run.of is itself WeakMap-backed — the difference is that the state and its ordering now live inside one object that owns them. #106 extends the same pattern in both directions. Run's rejected-envelope retention is ECMAScript-private state under the same consume-once discipline (stored as an isolated clone, taken exactly once), and eligibility is deliberately not Run's to decide — delegation.ts decides it, which is why the check ordering that makes the retention safe is documented on the check rather than on the field. Budget absorbed the wrap-up threshold as its own rule (nearsLiveStop, wrapUpNotice) instead of exposing a fraction for callers to compare against: the notice has to name the authority and spend of the ceiling about to bind, so one cascade at a scaled fraction resolves both the notice and the later refusal and they cannot describe different ceilings.

domain-events.label: Events/handoffs carry cross-boundary flow
domain-events.note: Handoff is a real transfer object: validated, redacted, policy-checked, provenance-bearing, and refused rather than silently degraded. CoordinationEvent is an immutable past-tense fact vocabulary over seven kinds. Events are export-only by design — coordination here is synchronous because a flow settles.

depth-rich-core.label: Depth: the Core Domain is genuinely rich, not CRUD
depth-rich-core.note: Trace evidence is now gated on both questions it raises rather than only the one the writer can answer: export accounting from the sink, and structure from reading the finished file back. That distinction is Core content, not plumbing — CONTEXT.md sells a finding that arrives carrying its own evidence, and a gate that certifies a file no reader can follow sells the claim without the thing. Contract identity by canonical digest, envelope-to-contract binding, artifact digest verification with realpath escape checks, single-use expiring approval receipts with binding digests, compositional injection, budget authority, and trace health kept separate from execution success and from verified outcome success. The admissibility seam adds another, and this review sharpened its mechanism: the selection eval no longer reassembles the tool's pre-spawn gates from imported predicates. Aggregate-level gates are still Core predicates the eval imports (the spawn gate, depth, concurrency, strict-trace config) and workflow's phase rules remain shared Core (validate-workflow.ts), but every per-mode refusal is now declared by the mode that enforces it and resolved through the table (preSpawnRefusalForParams), so the scored gate cannot drift from the enforced one by construction rather than by hand-maintained agreement, and a mode added to the table is covered without the eval changing. What the eval scores stays its own decision, named in one place (SCORED_PRE_SPAWN_CODES) instead of being implied by which predicates it happened to import. The distinction the declarations force is itself domain content: a refusal knowable before dispatch is the mode's declaration, while one only reachable mid-run (a probe that fails to start, a cycle stranding only later waves) stays in the handler and names a different moment.

depth-invariants-in-aggregates.label: Depth: invariants live inside aggregates, not services
depth-invariants-in-aggregates.note: Follows small-aggregates. Flow-level ordering — admission (preset expansion, mode detection, spawn gate, depth, concurrency, preset trust, preset preparation, strict-trace config, project-agent trust, spawn checkpoint, handler resolution, budget construction) and the settle sequence (blocking handoffs → preset formatting → reflexion → finalize checkpoint → trace finalize → strict-trace refusal → persistence last) — is enforced by the Flow aggregate's typed transitions: admission returns the only dispatch capability, dispatch returns the only thing that can settle, and both spend themselves. Rules like 'a refusal after the sink exists finalizes the trace with child_count 0' are internal to the aggregate. Named by tests/flow-lifecycle.test.ts and the checkpoint-skipped-before-spawn / settle-without-dispatch fault-manifest entries.

depth-language-consistency.label: Depth: ubiquitous language is consistent across docs, code, and tests
depth-language-consistency.note: A seventh blemish was found and fixed by the strict-trace review: 'trace health' was doing duty for both how much of the export was written and whether the export is a tree, two questions with different answers and different observers. CONTEXT.md now carries Trace structure beside Trace health with each on the other's Avoid list, and the code keeps them as separate members so neither can be reported as the other. CONTEXT.md carries Avoid lists; code and test names use the glossary's terms. A sixth blemish was found and fixed by the run-state review: the four states queued/running/completed/failed were named identically by three surfaces but derived three ways, so the ubiquitous language held while the derivation behind it forked — the failure mode this row exists to catch, appearing as agreeing words over disagreeing code rather than as competing words. CONTEXT.md now carries Run state, Settled names runSettled/runFailed as the question's one home and records why isFailed keeps a deliberately different contract, and the shared type is re-exported from run.ts rather than declared twice. A fifth blemish was found and fixed by the mode pre-spawn refusal review: that change claimed the bare phrase 'pre-spawn refusal' for a narrow new concept while six existing sites already used it for any refusal before spawning, and it simultaneously shipped 'pre-spawn declaration' as a second word for the same new concept. CONTEXT.md now carries Mode pre-spawn refusal with the bare phrase and the competing word both on its Avoid list, the mode files and the test speak the recorded term, and Mirror is sharpened to say a mirror is a second derivation that must be kept in agreement — preferring a declaration, which removes the second copy. A fourth blemish was found and fixed by the #106 review: #106 shipped the rejected-envelope concept with no glossary entry and under three competing words — 'rejected' (used in delegation.ts for both the always-returned trace evidence and the conditionally-retained Run field, which sit on opposite sides of the Return envelope entry's binding line), 'salvageable' (the discriminator), and 'unvalidated' (the label already shipped in preset-review.ts, troubleshooting.md, and the CHANGELOG). CONTEXT.md now carries Rejected envelope and Unvalidated claims — the outward-facing word won, so no user-visible sweep was needed — and delegation.ts, run.ts, preset-review.ts, troubleshooting.md, and the tests speak them, the discriminator having been renamed salvageable → claimsSurfaceable so the retired word does not survive in the code that retired it. One residue is deliberate: runner-budget.ts's 'distinguish salvage from loss' is the budget wrap-up sense (a run salvaged from forfeiture), not this concept, and is left alone. Three known blemishes remain. (1) 'contract' is overloaded between DelegationContract and RunModeContract. (2) topology.ts is named for mode topology but holds spec-parameter arithmetic, which is why it sits in Generic while the modes it is named after are Supporting. (3) 'the active child' is standard phrasing at 11 occurrences across docs/reference/flow-reference.md, docs/explanation (patterns, privacy-telemetry), docs/how-to/troubleshooting.md, examples, tests, budget.ts, and the schema.ts param descriptions (the README occurrence left with the Diátaxis reorg), though 'active' is on the Live entry's Avoid list; that sweep needs its own change, because fixing a subset breaks the README / flow-reference / TypeBox-params sync rule in AGENTS.md. Consequently budget.ts deliberately holds both vocabularies: the new API it introduces (stopsLiveRun and its JSDoc) takes the glossary term, while the pre-existing user-visible error cause keeps 'active child' so it stays consistent with the docs until they are swept together. Separately, the exported span attributes flow.budget.limit_* in trace-attributes.ts keep 'limit' as wire format - renaming them would break trace consumers, so they are a deliberate carve-out from the Budget ceiling Avoid list, not drift.

foreignImports._comment: adapters: modules where a foreign package type may legitimately be spoken - the anti-corruption layer, the extension registration surface, and the terminal views. debt: modules that still leak a foreign type into the domain and should not, each declaring in `imports` exactly which foreign packages it may name. scripts/domain-score.mjs enforces the ledger against the base revision AND against the tree: a module's actual foreign imports must equal its declared set, a declared package that is no longer imported must be deleted, and neither a new module nor a widened `imports` set may be added. So a new leak has to be fixed rather than recorded, and an existing entry cannot absorb one. The score's ACL row stays failed until the list is empty.
